evidence.trl_pathway: GAA at TRL 7 completing in 2 years and CIM at TRL 5 completing in 3 years are both plausible given semiconductor industry norms, though CIM's jump to deployment-ready in 3 years is moderately optimistic for an architecture-level technology. Hybrid bonding at TRL 6 over 2 years is reasonable given its dependency on GAA completion.
evidence.strategic_fidelity: While the portfolio includes technologies at moderate-to-high TRL (5-7), which is somewhat appropriate for technology leadership, the declared 기술선도 strategy would ideally include lower-TRL exploratory technologies (TRL 3-5) or emerging paradigms to establish frontier leadership; all three selections are relatively near-market, resembling a commercialization portfolio more than a pure technology leadership one.
evidence.competitive_awareness: The selection of GAA, hybrid bonding, and CIM reflects awareness of major semiconductor battlegrounds (TSMC, Samsung, Intel competition areas), but the roadmap lacks explicit differentiation rationale or timing designed around competitor gaps; the choices appear driven by technology importance rather than competitive positioning intelligence.
evidence.market_timing: For 기술선도 strategy, technologies should complete 1-2 years before the market boom to establish preemptive leadership. GAA completes 0.5yr after boom (slight miss), CIM completes 0.75yr after boom (adequate), but hybrid bonding completes 2.0 years after its boom window (significant miss), undermining the preemption logic.
evidence.patent_market_convergence: All three technologies (GAA, hybrid bonding, CIM) are in active patent filing zones and growing markets, suggesting general convergence awareness, but the roadmap does not articulate deliberate convergence-zone targeting — the selections appear motivated by strategic importance rather than explicit patent-market signal intersection analysis.
